name: New Jersey Resources
headline: A New Jersey gas utility whose margin is shielded from weather and whose fuel cost is passed to customers.
what_short: New Jersey gas utility, plus solar and gas marketing
what_it_does: New Jersey Resources owns New Jersey Natural Gas, which delivers gas to 588,975 customers in six New Jersey counties and supplies 54.8% of the group's five-year earnings. It also has a wholesale gas marketing business (24.5%), commercial solar projects (14.7%) and gas storage and pipeline interests (6.0%).
why_it_passed: The gas utility is a franchise, and a regulator-approved program (the Conservation Incentive Program) protects its margin from weather and usage.
Its gas cost is passed through to customers without markup, so commodity swings do not hit its earnings.
The regulator's order of November 2024 allowed 9.6% on equity with a 54.0% equity share, and a new case filed in June 2026 asks for 10.10%.
Group earnings averaged a 13.1% return on capital over five years, against 7.7% to 9.0% for three comparable gas utilities.
why_not_now: A regulator caps what this utility may earn, so the price is far above what that capped return justifies. The analysis values the whole business at -$18.22 to $15.91 a share ($5.26 to $37.87 counting only shareholders' money) against a price of $52.19. The best defensible case yields 3.20% a year, below the 5.43% a 30-year US Treasury bond pays.
watch: Debt is $3.7 billion, 58% of debt plus equity, and the company holds little cash and relies on short-term bank borrowing and commercial paper.
New Jersey's clean-energy plan, which pushes toward electrification, is a long-term political threat to gas distribution.
Cleanup of old gas plant sites is estimated at $144.3M to $200.2M, recovered through a regulator-approved rider.
